R0247.title: Session Token Replay
R0247.definition: Attackers replay stolen cookies, tokens, or session credentials from another device.
R0247.description:
Session token replay occurs when attackers steal cookies, access tokens, or refresh tokens and reuse them from another device or environment. Tokens may be obtained through malware, proxy logs, XSS, phishing, or endpoint compromise.

Without device binding, location checks, risk signals, or token rotation, attackers can bypass password and MFA checks. Defenses need token protection, abnormal session detection, and rapid revocation.
R0247.influence: Replayed session tokens bypass passwords and MFA, enabling account takeover, data export, and persistent access.

observables: Stolen cookies or tokens are replayed for login from foreign devices or locations
Session tokens unbound to device, location, or risk state are reused long-term
Accounts maintain persistent access without password or MFA
Token sources are linked to malware, proxy logs, or phishing sites
Anomalous sessions are accompanied by data export or privilege-escalation operations
